channel.title: The Catholic Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Catholic Review (catholicreview.org)

item.title: Trump signs funding deal to end partial government shutdown, negotiate over ICE
item.description: President Donald Trump signed into law a funding package to end the partial government shutdown Feb. 3, hours after its passage in the House, which included an agreement for funding for the Department of Homeland Security to be renegotiated to include new, stronger constraints on federal immigration officers.

item.title: U.S. bishops commemorate Black History Month: ‘Let us be faithful stewards of memory’
item.description: Two U.S. bishops Feb. 3 urged Catholics to be "faithful stewards of memory" and "courageous witnesses to truth" during Black History Month, observed in February.

item.title: Scripture is intended to speak to believers ‘in every age,’ pope says
item.description: Pope Leo XIV said Scripture is meant to speak directly to believers in today's world, emphasizing that the Bible is the word of God expressed through human authors during his weekly general audience.

item.title: Sister Joan Elias, leader in Catholic education, dies at 94
item.description: A funeral Mass for Grey Nun of the Sacred Heart Sister Joan Elias will be offered at 10 a.m. Feb. 7 at Redeemer Sisters’ Chapel in Huntingdon Valley, Pa. Sister Joan died Jan. 27. She was 94.

item.title: Vatican secretary of state prioritized dialogue during Denmark visit, archbishop says
item.description: During his recent visit to Denmark, Cardinal Pietro Parolin declined an invitation to sign a joint declaration regarding Greenland's sovereignty, in the hopes of maintaining neutrality and fostering dialogue, said Danish Bishop Czeslaw Kozon of Copenhagen.

item.title: Haitian Catholics in U.S. relieved, yet wary, after judge temporarily halts end of protected status
item.description: A Haitian Catholic chaplain serving in the U.S. said he and fellow Haitian Catholics are welcoming a last-minute reprieve from threats of deportation -- but its members are still weighing options as the Trump administration cracks down on immigration, while Haiti continues to spiral into chaos.

item.title: America’s first basilica marks a century
item.description: At a Feb. 1 Mass honoring the Basilica of St. Mary's centennial, local Church leaders spoke about its architectural and liturgical beauty, but even more so about the church's "living stones" who weren't present in 1926: its parishioners.

item.title: Exploring Catherine O’Hara’s Catholic roots
item.description: Catholic faith was not part of comedian Catherine O'Hara's public-facing work and personality.

item.title: One day after desecration, California school holds reparation Mass
item.description: When Principal Cyril Cruz arrived at Holy Innocents School in Long Beach early on the morning of Feb. 2, she discovered a scene of "desecration": trash, food, several Virgin Mary statues broken and Catholic missal books spilled onto the floor. The tabernacle was significantly damaged.

item.title: Amid U.S. foreign aid cuts, bishops call for solidarity between American, African Catholics
item.description: Amid severe cuts in U.S. foreign aid, Catholic bishops an ocean apart are advocating for deeper bonds between the U.S. and the peoples of the African continent -- with God-given human dignity as central to that summons.
